deviations: File writing: the sheet says to work in a scratch subfolder, but my brief forbade writing any file, so I wrote none. Gazette, bill and record PDFs and DOCs were read in memory: PDFKit opened them from the URL, and textutil read the DOC from a stdin pipe. The harness saved two oversized command outputs (Open Knesset CSV extracts and a Nevo page) to its own tool-results folder; I did not create them.

Court material, seq 39: the bill's explanatory notes (13_ls1_292333.PDF) contain a paragraph summarising a High Court judgment on the earlier provision. I disregarded that paragraph and coded from the enacted text and the rest of the notes. No page about a court case was opened.

Court material, other: the Hebrew Wikisource page for Basic Law: The Judiciary has a header link to a later judgment, and its current text reflects later amendments. I did not follow the link and did not use that page for the as-passed text; I used the 1984 gazette PDF instead. My first web search returned a results summary that mentioned court litigation about the 1981 dismissal power; I opened none of those pages and used nothing from them.

Search budget: the session's web-search budget was exhausted after two searches, so press reports of tallies or readings could not be searched for. The National Library historical-newspaper site refused direct requests (HTTP 403).

Sources beyond the sheet's list, all Knesset records: Open Knesset mirrors of the bill table (pipelines/data/bills/kns_bill, kns_documentbill), used to find bill numbers and bill-document URLs; the plenum agenda tables (pipelines/data/plenum/kns_plmsessionitem, kns_plenumsession, kns_documentplenumsession), used for reading dates and record-file IDs; the status code table (pipelines/data/knesset/kns_status). Internet Archive captures (2003) of the Knesset's 'Factional and Government Make-Up' pages for the 9th-13th Knessets gave government composition. The live Knesset site redirects to a geo-block page.

Encyclopedia: the English Wikipedia articles on the 18th, 20th, 22nd, 24th, 25th and 26th governments were read as a cross-check. Only for seq 19 is one cited, because the Knesset page does not fix the coalition on 19 May 1981 precisely.

Other text sources: archived Nevo copies of Basic Law: The Government (1968 and 1992) were read only to understand the provisions amended by seqs 39, 42 and 48 (s. 5(b1), s. 21(d), the previous s. 9). The seq 22 gazette PDF (10_lsr_211737.PDF, capture 20240727184959) is not listed in the sheet; I reached it from the Wikisource page header.

Not found, final-vote records: the Knesset record files for the final-vote sittings of seqs 19, 25, 28, 35, 39, 42, 45, 48 and 51 have no Internet Archive capture. Files checked: 9_ptm_254051/258235/249860; 11_ptm_530879/235928; 12_ptm_531702/236639; 12_ptm_531974/236743; 13_ptm_532404, 532436, 532443, 532423, 532429. The NYU Faculty Digital Archive holds only settlement-related plenum excerpts, and its search found none of these sittings. Tallies and coalition_only are therefore blank for those nine.

Not found, first readings: the records of the first-reading sittings for seq 31 (18 and 25 June 1991) and seq 39 (14 and 28 Nov 1994) are not archived. In each case the agenda data show the bill at first reading on two dates, one inside and one outside thirty days of the final vote, so expedited is blank for both.
Not found, explanatory notes: bill PDFs are archived only for seq 22 (1978 government bill) and seq 39. Notes for seqs 19, 25, 28, 31, 35, 42, 45, 48 and 51 were not reachable.
Partial vote records: seq 22 and seq 31 have records but name no voters (a show of hands with totals only, and an electronic tally of 16-0-0), so coalition_only is blank for them as well.

Text-layer quirks in gazette footnotes: seq 42 reads '22 בינואר 1966' and bill '2562' (the Knesset bill table gives 2362); seq 45 reads the bill date's year as התשנ"ד; seq 51 reads '2 ו במרס' (the Hebrew date כ"א באדר התשנ"ו is 12 March 1996).
